facts.statement: Dacentrurus fossils date from the Late Jurassic to the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Jurassic, - Early Cretaceous

facts.statement: The genus name was changed to Dacentrurus in 1902 because Omosaurus was already in use for a phytosaur.
facts.quote: In 1902 the genus was renamed Dacentrurus because the name Omosaurus had already been used for a phytosaur in 1856.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus means "tail full of points" and is an extinct stegosaurian dinosaur from Europe living between 154 and 140 million years ago.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus (meaning "tail full of points") is an extinct genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic and perhaps Early Cretaceous (154–140 million years ago) of Europe.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus is one of the largest known stegosaurs, reaching lengths of 8 to 9 meters and weights of up to 7.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus is among the largest known stegosaurs, measuring around 8 - 9 m long and weighing up to 5 - 7.4 MT.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named and described the type species in 1875 as Omosaurus armatus.
facts.quote: Owen named and described the remains in 1875 as the type species Omosaurus armatus.

facts.statement: The original genus name Omosaurus was derived from the Greek word for "upper arm" due to the robust humerus.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Greek ὦμος, omos, "upper arm", in reference to the robust humerus.

facts.statement: The specific name armatus refers to a large spike that Owen believed was located on the upper arm.
facts.quote: The specific name armatus can mean "armed" in Latin and in this case refers to a large spike that Owen assumed was present on the upper arm.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation dating to the late Kimmeridgian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, NHMUK PV OR 46013, was found in a layer of the Kimmeridge Clay Formation dating from the late Kimmeridgian.

facts.statement: The holotype skeleton lacks the skull and consists only of postcranial elements.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a postcranial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: An almost complete left forelimb was found in a separate loam clump associated with the main specimen.
facts.quote: Also an almost complete left forelimb was contained by another loam clump.

facts.statement: Frederick Augustus Lucas renamed the genus Dacentrurus in 1902.
facts.quote: In 1902, Frederick Augustus Lucas renamed the genus into Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: The name Dacentrurus is derived from Greek words meaning "full of points on the tail".
facts.quote: The name is derived from Greek δα~, da~, "very" or "full of", κέντρον, kentron, "point", and οὐρά, oura, "tail".

facts.statement: Remains attributed to Dacentrurus were reported from a bonebed in France dating to the earliest Cretaceous in 2021.
facts.quote: In 2021, remains attributed to Dacentrurus sensu lato were reported from the earliest Cretaceous (Berriasian) Angeac-Charente bonebed of France.

facts.statement: In 2024, eleven specimens from France, Portugal, and Spain were assigned to Dacentrurus armatus.
facts.quote: In 2024, 11 specimens (including the holotype and referred material of Miragaia longicollum) from France, Portugal, and Spain were assigned to Dacentrurus armatus.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Miragaia longicollum is a junior synonym of Dacentrurus armatus.
facts.quote: Some researchers suggest that Miragaia longicollum represents a junior synonym of this taxon.

facts.statement: The limited fossil record makes the appearance of Dacentrurus uncertain and its relationships with other stegosaurs contentious.
facts.quote: Finds of this animal have been limited, so much of its appearance is uncertain and its relationship with other members of the Dacentrurinae are contentious.

facts.statement: Edwin Hennig moved several Omosaurus species into Dacentrurus in 1915, creating multiple species within the genus.
facts.quote: In 1915 Edwin Hennig moved most Omosaurus species to Dacentrurus, resulting in a Dacentrurus hastiger, Dacentrurus durobrivensis, Dacentrurus phillipsi and a Dacentrurus lennieri.

facts.statement: The species Omosaurus phillipsii is considered a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: O. phillipsii has been considered a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus vetustus was once assigned to the genus Lexovisaurus but was later rejected from that genus and is now the type species of Eoplophysis.
facts.quote: D. vetustus, earlier indicated as Omosaurus (Dacentrurus) vetustus by von Huene, was included with Lexovisaurus as a Lexovisaurus vetustus in 1983, but that assignment was rejected with both editions of the Dinosauria, and O. vetustus is now the type species of "Eoplophysis".

facts.statement: Dacentrurus was the first stegosaur known from articulated remains and became the default classification for most European stegosaur finds.
facts.quote: Due to the fact it represented the best known stegosaurian species from Europe, the first known from articulated remains, most stegosaur discoveries in this area were referred to Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus lived approximately 145 million years ago during the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary and was prevalent in the Iberian range.
facts.quote: This discovery was considered significant because it would demonstrate both the intra-specific variability of Dacentrurus armatus, and the strong prevalence of Dacentrurus in the Iberian range during the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary, approximately 145 million years ago.

facts.statement: A 125-millimetre-long egg attributed to Dacentrurus represents the first egg ever associated with any stegosaur.
facts.quote: A longitudinally sectioned egg, with a length of 125 millimetres, from Portugal has been attributed to Dacentrurus, the first associated with any stegosaur.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus was one of the largest stegosaurs, with specimens reaching 8 to 9 meters in length, 1.8 meters in hip height, and 5 to 7.4 metric tons in body mass.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus was one of the largest genera of stegosaurs along with Stegosaurus, with some specimens having been estimated to reach 8 - 9 m in length, 1.8 m in hip height and 5 - 7.4 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The neck of Dacentrurus consisted of twelve vertebrae.
facts.quote: The neck consists of twelve vertebrae.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus possessed at least two pairs of stocky spines with expanded bases and four pairs of long spines with small bases on its tail.
facts.quote: At least two pair of stocky spines are present with an expanded base and four pairs of long spines with a small base on the tail.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus had a massive humerus with an enormous deltopectoral crest that served as an attachment for powerful musculature.
facts.quote: The forelimb of Dacentrurus contains a massive humerus, its shaft protruding in an enormous deltopectoral crest, the attachment for a powerful musculature.

facts.statement: The holotype pelvis of Dacentrurus had a right ilium measuring 1048 millimetres in length and a total width of 1493 millimetres across the front blades of both ilia.
facts.quote: The right ilium has a maximal length of 1048 millimetres. Measured over the front blades of both ilia, the pelvis is 1493 millimetres wide.

facts.statement: It is debated whether material from the Villar del Arzobispo Formation belongs to Dacentrurus or Miragaia, as 2019 research showed stronger affinities to Miragaia.
facts.quote: However, new referred material of Miragaia described in 2019 shows stronger affinities to the Villar del Arzobispo material than to the holotype material of Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: Recent studies argue that Alcovasaurus is not synonymous with Dacentrurus and should be classified as a separate species of Miragaia.
facts.quote: In their re-description of the specimen MG 4863, Costa et al. (2025) argued that the two taxa are not synonymous based on comparison with the Dacentrurus holotype and that Alcovasaurus should be included as a second species of Miragaia.

facts.statement: The holotype of Dacentrurus armatus includes a small, blunt, asymmetrical plate on the neck or front back.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen of Dacentrurus armatus contained a small blunt asymmetrical neck or front back plate.

facts.statement: The preserved tail spike in the holotype has a maximum length of 456 millimetres.
facts.quote: This spike has a preserved maximum length of 456 millimetres.

facts.statement: The maximum base width of the tail spike is 118 millimetres.
facts.quote: Its maximal base width is 118 millimetres.

facts.statement: The better preserved left tail spine shows many small notches along its inner edge.
facts.quote: The better preserved left spine shows that the inner edge has many small notches.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus has sometimes been depicted with a shoulder spike similar to that of Kentrosaurus, though this is unconfirmed.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus has sometimes been portrayed with a spike growing near the shoulder, similar to Kentrosaurus.

facts.statement: Large olecranon horns on the ulnae and large deltoid crests on the humerus suggest a powerful deltoid muscle capable of strong flexion and abduction.
facts.quote: Combined with large deltoid crests on the humerus, they suggest a powerful musculus deltoideus making a strong humeral flexion and abduction possible.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus likely used its anchored forelimbs and sweeping tail thagomizer to defend against large theropods like Torvosaurus.
facts.quote: The forelimbs could then be firmly anchored on the ground while the tail was forcefully swept from side to side, allowing the thagomizer to defend against large theropod predators, such as Torvosaurus.

facts.statement: Some specimens of Dacentrurus are estimated to reach lengths of 7 to 8 meters and weigh up to 5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que algunos especímenes alcanzan longitudes de 7-8 metros y que pesan hasta 5 toneladas.

facts.statement: Despite being often described as small, Dacentrurus had a 1.5-meter wide pelvis, indicating it was among the largest stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Muchos libros afirman que Dacentrurus era un pequeño estegosáurido, cuando en realidad tiene una pelvis de 1,5 metros de ancho que indica que Dacentrurus estaba entre los más grandes.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus had narrow, sharper plates along its back and tail used for protection compared to other stegosaurs.
facts.quote: A lo largo del lomo y cola, tenía unas placas estrechas, más afiladas que las de otros estegosáuridos, usadas para protección.

facts.statement: Although similar in proportions to Stegosaurus, Dacentrurus likely had two rows of small plates on its neck and two rows of longer spikes along its tail.
facts.quote: Aunque se considera que Dacentrurus tiene las mismas proporciones que el Stegosaurus, se sabe que su configuración de placa y espinas es bastante diferente, ya que probablemente tenía dos hileras de placas pequeñas en el cuello y dos hileras de espinas más largas a lo largo de su cola.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus armatus lived during the late Jurassic period, approximately 157 to 152 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus armatus (gr. "cola puntiaguda equipado con armadura") es la única especie conocida del género Dacentrurus de dinosaurio tireóforo estegosáurido, que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente entre 157 y 152 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense y Kimmeridgiense, en lo que hoy es Europa.

facts.statement: The type species Omosaurus armatus was named in 1875 based on a skeleton found in England.
facts.quote: Su especie tipo, Omosaurus armatus, fue nombrada en 1875, basándose en un esqueleto encontrado en Inglaterra.

facts.statement: The genus was renamed Dacentrurus in 1902 because the name Omosaurus was already used for a crocodile.
facts.quote: En 1902, el género fue renombrado como Dacentrurus porque el nombre Omosaurus ya había sido usado por un cocodrilo.

facts.statement: The genus Dacentrurus was established by Lucas in 1902.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Lucas, 1902

facts.statement: The species D. armatus was originally described by Owen in 1875.
facts.quote: species_authority: Owen,1875

facts.statement: Dacentrurus is classified in the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: Dacentrurus belongs to the subfamily Dacentrurinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Dacentrurinae

facts.statement: Studies in 2008 and 2010 determined that Dacentrurus forms the clade Dacentrurinae with Miragaia longicollum as its sister species.
facts.quote: In 2008 and 2010 studies determined it as forming the clade Dacentrurinae with its sister species Miragaia longicollum.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Dacentrurus is a basal or derived stegosaurid, with later analyses showing it to be relatively derived.
facts.quote: Earlier often considered to have been a rather basal stegosaurid, Dacentrurus was by more extensive cladistic analyses shown to be relatively derived.

facts.statement: It is currently undetermined whether Dacentrurus actually possessed a shoulder spike similar to Kentrosaurus.
facts.quote: Whether this portrayal is accurate or not is not yet determined.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus had a small head with a flattened beak and aligned molars on both sides for crushing plants.
facts.quote: Presentaba una pequeña cabeza con un pico aplanado que poseía muelas alineadas a ambos lados para triturar las plantas que comía.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus had relatively short hind limbs but relatively long forelimbs, largely due to a long forearm.
facts.quote: La extremidad posterior era bastante corta, pero la extremidad anterior relativamente larga, en gran parte debido a un antebrazo largo.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus had an especially wide intestine and a large rump, indicated by exceptionally wide centers of dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Para un estegosáurido, el intestino era especialmente ancho, y una grupa grande también está indicada por un centro de las vértebras dorsales excepcionalmente anchos.

facts.statement: Richard Owen described Dacentrurus armatus in 1875 as the first known stegosaur.
facts.quote: Cuando fue descrito por Richard Owen en 1875 como Omosaurus armatus, fue el primer estegosáurido conocido

facts.statement: On May 23, 1874, James Shopland informed Richard Owen that fossil bones were found in the Swindon Brick & Tile Company's clay pit in Wiltshire.
facts.quote: El 23 de mayo de 1874, James Shopland de Swindon Brick & Tyle Company informaron al profesor Richard Owen que su pozo de arcilla, la Gran Cantera Swindon debajo de Old Swindon Hill en Swindon de Wiltshire, había vuelto a producir un esqueleto fósil

facts.statement: The fossil specimen was found encased in a clay nodule eight feet high.
facts.quote: Owen envió a William Davies para asegurar el espécimen, que resultó estar encerrado en un nódulo de arcilla de ocho pies de alto

facts.statement: The fossil fragments were transported to London in crates weighing a total of three tons.
facts.quote: Estos fueron en algún momento transportados a Londres en cajas con un peso total de tres toneladas

facts.statement: The holotype BMNH 46013 was found in the Kimmeridge Clay Formation dating to the Late Kimmeridgian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, BMNH 46013, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Kimmeridge Clay que data del Kimmeridgiano tardío

facts.statement: The generic name Dacentrurus derives from the Greek word for 'upper arm', referring to its robust humerus.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del griego μος, omos , "brazo superior", en referencia al húmero robusto

facts.statement: The specific name armatus means 'armed' in Latin, referring to a large spike Owen believed was present on the upper arm.
facts.quote: El nombre específico armatus puede significar "armado" en latín y en este caso se refiere a un gran pincho que Owen supuso que estaba presente en la parte superior del brazo

facts.statement: The main fragment of the nodule contains the pelvis, six posterior dorsal vertebrae, all sacral vertebrae, eight anterior caudal vertebrae, a right femur, and some loose vertebrae.
facts.quote: El fragmento principal del nódulo contiene la pelvis, una serie de seis vértebras dorsales posteriores, todas las sacras y las ocho vértebras caudales anteriores, un fémur derecho y algunas vértebras sueltas

facts.statement: In total, thirteen detached vertebrae are present in the material.
facts.quote: En total, trece vértebras desprendidas están presentes en el material

facts.statement: An almost complete left forelimb was contained within another group of marl.
facts.quote: También una extremidad anterior izquierda casi completa estaba contenida por otro grupo de marga

facts.statement: Fossil evidence of this dinosaur is found throughout Europe, including England, France, Spain, and five skeletons found in Portugal.
facts.quote: La evidencia fósil de este dinosaurio se encuentran por toda Europa, tanto en Inglaterra, Wiltshire y Dorset, incluyendo un vértebra asignada a D. armatus en Weymouth, así como en Francia, España y los últimos cinco esqueletos encontrados en Portugal

facts.statement: Several species originally assigned to Dacentrurus were later reclassified, including D. durobrivensis (now Lexovisaurus durobrivensis), D. phillipsi, and D. vetustus (now Lexovisaurus vetustus).
facts.quote: Otras especie fueron sido asignadas al género Dacentrurus para luego cambiar, Estas incluyen a D. durobrivensis, hoy Lexovisaurus durobrivensis, D. phillipsi, incluido a veces equivocadamente con Priodontognathus phillipsi, debido a que tiene el mismo nombre de especie y una historia confusa, y D. vetustus, incluido en Lexovisaurus vetustus

facts.statement: A pair of spine bases found in Kimmeridge clay near Wootton Bassett by William Cunnington is part of the Natural History Museum collection.
facts.quote: Parte de la colección del Museo Británico de Historia Natural es el espécimen BMNH 46321, un par de bases de espinas encontradas en la arcilla Kimmeridge por William Cunnington cerca del ferrocarril Great Western cerca de Wootton Bassett.

facts.statement: Richard Owen named Omosaurus hastiger in 1877 based on spine bases found near Wootton Bassett.
facts.quote: A partir de estos Owen en 1877 nombraron a Omosaurus hastiger

facts.statement: John Whitaker Hulke named Omosaurus durobrivensis in 1887 based on specimen BMNH R1989 found at Tanholt near Eye, Cambridgeshire.
facts.quote: En 1887, John Whitaker Hulke llamado Omosaurus durobrivensis basado en el espécimen BMNH R1989 encontrado en Tanholt , cerca de Eye, Cambridgeshire

facts.statement: Fossils from Fletton, Peterborough, were assigned to the separate genus Lexovisaurus in 1956.
facts.quote: En 1956 se convirtió en el género separado Lexovisaurus.

facts.statement: Harry Govier Seeley named Omosaurus phillipsii in 1893 based on femur specimen YM 498.
facts.quote: En 1893, Harry Govier Seeley nombró a Omosaurus phillipsii, basado en un fémur, espécimen YM 498

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene named Omosaurus vetustus in 1910 based on femur specimen OUM J.14000 found on the west bank of the River Cherwell.
facts.quote: En 1910 Friedrich von Huene nombró a Omosaurus vetustus, basado en el espécimen OUM J.14000, un fémur encontrado en la orilla oeste del río Cherwell

facts.statement: Franz Nopcsa named Omosaurus lennieri in 1911 based on a partial skeleton found in 1899 at Argiles d'Octeville near Cap de la Hève in Normandy, France.
facts.quote: En 1911 Franz Nopcsa nombró a Omosaurus lennieri, el epíteto que honra a Gustave Lennier, basado en un esqueleto parcial en 1899 encontrado en Kimmeridgian Argiles d'Octeville cerca de Cap de la Hève en Normandía, Francia.

facts.statement: The partial skeleton of Omosaurus lennieri was destroyed during the Allied bombing of Caen in 1944.
facts.quote: El espécimen sería destruido durante el bombardeo aliado de Caen en 1944.

facts.statement: Frederick Augustus Lucas renamed the genus Omosaurus to Dacentrurus in 1902.
facts.quote: En 1902, Frederick Augustus Lucas renombró el género en Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: Lucas initially only created a new combination name for the type species Omosaurus armatus.
facts.quote: Lucas solo dio un nuevo nombre de combinación para la especie tipo Omosaurus armatus

facts.statement: Edwin Hennig moved most Omosaurus species to Dacentrurus in 1915, resulting in the species D. hastiger, D. durobrivensis, D. phillipsi, and D. lennieri.
facts.quote: en 1915 Edwin Hennig movió la mayoría de las especies de Omosaurus a Dacentrurus, lo que resultó en Dacentrurus hastiger, Dacentrurus durobrivensis, Dacentrurus phillipsi y Dacentrurus lennieri.

facts.statement: D. vetustus was assigned to Lexovisaurus in 1983, but this was rejected in both editions of Dinosauria, and O. vetustus is now the type species of Eoplophysis.
facts.quote: D. vetustus, anteriormente indicado como Omosaurus ( Dacentrurus ) vetustus por von Huene, se incluyó con Lexovisaurus como Lexovisaurus vetustus en 1983, pero esa asignación fue rechazada con ambas ediciones de Dinosauria, y O. vetustus es ahora la especie tipo de Eoplophysis.

facts.statement: Most European stegosaurid discoveries were historically attributed to Dacentrurus because it was one of the best-known species in Europe.
facts.quote: Debido a que representa una de las especie de estegosáuridos más conocidas de Europa, la mayoría de los descubrimientos de estegosáuridos en esta área fueron referidos a Dacentrurus.

facts.statement: Fossils attributed to Dacentrurus have been found in Wiltshire and Dorset in southern England, including a vertebra from Weymouth.
facts.quote: Esto incluyó hallazgos en Wiltshire y Dorset en el sur de Inglaterra, entre ellos una vértebra atribuida a D. armatus en Weymouth.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dacentrurus have been found in France, Spain, and Portugal, where five more recent skeletons were discovered.
facts.quote: Fósiles de Francia y España y otros cinco esqueletos más recientes de Portugal.

facts.statement: The most complete skeletons of Dacentrurus are the holotypes of D. armatus and D. lennieri.
facts.quote: Los únicos esqueletos más completos fueron los holotipos de D. armatus y D. lennieri.

facts.statement: Eggs attributed to Dacentrurus have been discovered in Portugal.
facts.quote: También se han descubierto huevos atribuidos a Dacentrurus en Portugal.

facts.statement: In 2013, Alberto Cobos and Francisco Gascó described stegosaurid vertebral remains found at the "Barranco Conejero" locality in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation in Riodeva, Teruel, Spain.
facts.quote: En 2013, Alberto Cobos y Francisco Gascó describieron restos vertebrales de estegosáuridos, que se encontraron agrupados en la localidad "Barranco Conejero" de la Formación Villar del Arzobispo en Riodeva, Teruel, España.

facts.statement: A discovery in Spain dated to approximately 145 million years ago at the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary demonstrated both the intraspecific variability of Dacentrurus armatus and its strong prevalence in the Iberian range.
facts.quote: Este descubrimiento se consideró significativo porque demostraría tanto la variabilidad intraespecífica de Dacentrurus armatus como la fuerte prevalencia de Dacentrurus En el rango ibérico lo coloca en el límite Jurásico-Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 145 millones de años.

facts.statement: In 2024, Sánchez-Fenollosa and colleagues systematically studied one of Europe's most complete stegosaur skeletons and conducted a comprehensive taxonomic evaluation of all non-Stegosaurus material from Late Jurassic Europe.
facts.quote: En 2024, Sánchez-Fenollosa y colaboradores. estudiaron sistemáticamente uno de los esqueletos de estegosaurio más completos de Europa y realizaron una evaluación taxonómica exhaustiva de todo el material no atribuido a Stegosaurus del Jurásico Superior de Europa.

facts.statement: Besides the type material from England, 11 specimens from France, Portugal, and Spain can be assigned to Dacentrurus armatus and considered part of its type series.
facts.quote: Además del material tipo (Inglaterra), 11 especímenes de Francia, Portugal y España pueden asignarse a Dacentrurus armatus y considerarse parte del hipodigma.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus was the first stegosaurid with good remains discovered, whereas earlier finds like Paranthodon, Regnosaurus, and Craterosaurus were too limited to be recognized as a distinct new group.
facts.quote: Dacentrurus fue el primer estegosáurido del que se han descubierto buenos restos, los hallazgos anteriores como Paranthodon, Regnosaurus y Craterosaurus eran demasiado limitados para ser directamente reconocibles como la representación de un nuevo grupo distintivo.

facts.statement: Dacentrurus is generally assigned to the family Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: En el Dacentrurus' generalmente se asigna a Stegosauridae.

facts.statement: While previously often considered a basal stegosaurid, Dacentrurus was shown by extensive cladistic analyses in 2008 and 2010 to be relatively derived, forming the clade Dacentrurinae with its sister species Miragaia longicollum.
facts.quote: Anteriormente a menudo se consideraba que era un estegosáurido bastante basal, Dacentrurus fue por análisis cladísticos más extensos en 2008 y 2010 que se demostró que era relativamente derivado, formando el clado Dacentrurinae con su especie hermana Miragaia longicollum.

facts.statement: According to Paul Sereno, the Dacentrurinae were the sister group to Stegosaurus and the Stegosaurinae.
facts.quote: Los Dacentrurinae eran el grupo hermano de Stegosaurus, Stegosaurinae según Paul Sereno.

facts.statement: In the Iberian range, Dacentrurus lived at the Jurassic-Cretaceous boundary, approximately 145 million years ago.
facts.quote: En el rango ibérico lo coloca en el límite Jurásico-Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 145 millones de años.

facts.statement: The genus Dacentrurus lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Barremian, between 154.8 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Barremian (154.8 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Dacentrurus is the subfamily Dacentrurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dacentrurinae

facts.statement: The family of the genus Dacentrurus is Stegosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Stegosauridae

facts.statement: The class of the genus Dacentrurus is Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Dacentrurus is Dacentrurus armatus.
facts.quote: Type species: Dacentrurus armatus

facts.statement: In 2008, Susannah Maidment adopted a radically different approach by limiting the material of D. armatus to its holotype.
facts.quote: Un planteamiento radicalmente diferente fue tomado en 2008 por Susannah Maidment que limitó el material de D. armatus a su holotipo.

facts.statement: Susannah Maidment considered most named species, including "Astrodon" pusillus from Portugal based on stegosaurid fossils, to be dubious.
facts.quote: La mayoría de las especies nombradas, entre ellas "Astrodon" pusillus de Portugal, basada en fósiles de estegosáuridos, las considera dudosa.

facts.statement: Maidment considered continental European specimens possibly a separate species but assigned them to Dacentrurus sp. because the material was too limited to establish distinctive traits.
facts.quote: Ella consideró que los especímenes de Europa continental posiblemente fueran una especie separada, pero como era demasiado limitado para establecer rasgos distintivos, se lo asignó a Dacentrurus sp..

facts.statement: Sánchez-Fenollosa and colleagues concluded that there are no morphological criteria to distinguish two dacentrurine taxa in Late Jurassic Europe, proposing Miragaia longicollum as a synonym of Dacentrurus armatus.
facts.quote: Sánchez-Fenollosa y colaboradores. estudiaron sistemáticamente uno de los esqueletos de estegosaurio más completos de Europa y realizaron una evaluación taxonómica exhaustiva de todo el material no atribuido a Stegosaurus del Jurásico Superior de Europa. Los investigadores principalmente concluyeron: No existen criterios morfológicos para distinguir dos taxones de dacentrurinos en el Jurásico Superior de Europa (se propone a Miragaia longicollum como un sinónimo de Dacentrurus armatus).

facts.statement: No morphological criteria support the taxonomic combination Dacentrurus (= Miragaia) longispinus, so the species longispinus from Late Jurassic North America is returned to the genus Alcovasaurus.
facts.quote: Ningún criterio morfológico respalda la combinación taxonómica Dacentrurus (= Miragaia) longispinus. Por lo tanto, la especie longispinus (Jurásico Superior, EE. UU.) se devuelve al género Alcovasaurus.

rejected.statement: The type species Dacentrurus armatus was named in 1875 from a skeleton found in a clay pit in Swindon, England.
rejected.quote: Its type species, D. armatus, was named in 1875 as Omosaurus armatus, based on a skeleton found in a clay pit in the Kimmeridge Clay in Swindon, England.
